memory_lessons.applicability: Use these results as context for testing SIMD and row-parallel interaction; they do not predict the combined variant's timing.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial r-k-c, serial r-k-c with SIMD, and row-parallel r-k-c variants were all valid. Their measured means were 0.076396257 s, 0.073052032 s, and 0.009476691 s respectively; these results do not isolate SIMD's effect when combined with row parallelism.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the combined row-parallel and SIMD variant on all official sizes, check overwrite behavior and oracle tolerance, and compare repeated native n=1024 timings with the row-parallel result.

proposal.hypothesis: The serial r-k-c variant was valid at a 0.076396257 s mean, and adding an explicit c-dimension SIMD directive without threads measured 0.073052032 s; row-parallel r-k-c measured 0.009476691 s. This experiment tests whether combining static row parallelism, capped by the caller's thread count, with contiguous c-dimension SIMD improves on row parallelism alone. Each output element retains ascending-k accumulation and C is cleared on every call. The combined effect remains unmeasured.

retained: Replace fixed-size dispatch with runtime dimensions so the kernel handles valid sizes without specializing to the official benchmark sizes.
Clear the complete output before accumulating with an r-k-c traversal, preserving ascending-k accumulation for each output element.
Parallelize independent output rows with static scheduling and at most min(n, threads) workers; use a serial path when the available worker count is at most one.
Apply OpenMP SIMD to the innermost contiguous c traversal as the single follow-up interaction test.
